facts.name: Mayapple
facts.color: White flower hidden under the leaves
facts.notes: Umbrella-like leaves that carpet the woodland floor in spring, then die back by midsummer. Spreads into colonies.

sources.title: Penn State Extension: Spring Ephemerals for Residential Gardens
sources.note: Virginia bluebell foliage dies back by summer, so interplant with hostas or ferns; mayapple goes dormant in summer, so pair it with ferns or late-summer flowers.

companions.why: Commonly found with wild columbine, wild ginger, wild geranium, woodland phlox and mayapple.
